chapter_title: Learning Graphs, Interoperability Standards, and Access at Scale
learning_objective: The learner will solve six problems by selecting exactly the set of ready concepts in a 16-concept learning graph for a given set of mastered concepts, correctly answering at least five of six on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: graph-model **sim-id:** ready-concepts-finder
**Library:** vis-network
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** solve
**Learning Objective:** The learner will solve six problems by selecting exactly the set of ready concepts in a 16-concept learning graph for a given set of mastered concepts, correctly answering at least five of six on the first attempt. **Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/automating-instructional-design/tree/main/docs/sims/learning-dependency-network
**Prerequisites:** learning dependency, foundational concept, directed acyclic graph, learning path, the ready rule (all defined in the section "Learning Graphs: Maps of Concepts" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of 6 problems, the learner selects the set of nodes they judge to be ready and submits it. A selection is correct when it equals the "Ready set" in Content exactly, with no missing and no extra nodes. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Selecting a node to read its description is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A concept is ready as soon as one prerequisite is mastered. (2) A concept already mastered can still be ready. (3) Only one concept can be ready at a time. **Instructional Rationale:** Solving a ready-set problem applies the rule step by step: for each unmastered node, check every direct prerequisite. Problems with an empty mastered set, several ready nodes, and a single ready node show the range of cases. **Content:** Sixteen concepts taken from this book's learning graph (provenance below), with their direct prerequisites. An arrow from a concept points to its prerequisites. | Concept | Direct prerequisites | |---|---| | Artificial Intelligence | none | | Exponential Growth | none | | AI Capability | Artificial Intelligence | | Machine Learning | Artificial Intelligence | | Doubling Time | Exponential Growth | | AI Benchmark | AI Capability | | Large Language Model | Machine Learning | | METR | AI Benchmark | | AI Agent | Large Language Model | | Benchmark Task Suite | METR, AI Benchmark | | Task Horizon | METR, AI Capability | | 50 Percent Time Horizon | Task Horizon | | Human Working Time | Task Horizon | | Long-Running Task | Task Horizon, AI Agent | | Task Success Rate | Task Horizon | | Five-Month Doubling | Task Horizon, 50 Percent Time Horizon, Human Working Time, Benchmark Task Suite, Long-Running Task, Task Success Rate, Doubling Time | The ready rule: a concept is ready when it is not mastered and every one of its direct prerequisites is mastered. Six problems: | # | Mastered concepts | Ready set | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | none | Artificial Intelligence; Exponential Growth | Only concepts with no prerequisites can be ready when nothing is mastered. | | 2 | Artificial Intelligence; Exponential Growth | AI Capability; Machine Learning; Doubling Time | Each depends only on a mastered concept. | | 3 | Artificial Intelligence; Exponential Growth; AI Capability; Machine Learning; Doubling Time | AI Benchmark; Large Language Model | Each depends only on mastered concepts; METR still needs AI Benchmark. | | 4 | Artificial Intelligence; Exponential Growth; AI Capability; Machine Learning; Doubling Time; AI Benchmark; Large Language Model; METR; AI Agent | Benchmark Task Suite; Task Horizon | Both depend only on mastered concepts; Long-Running Task still needs Task Horizon. | | 5 | All nine from problem 4, plus Benchmark Task Suite and Task Horizon | 50 Percent Time Horizon; Human Working Time; Long-Running Task; Task Success Rate | All four depend only on Task Horizon, and on AI Agent for the Long-Running Task. | | 6 | All fifteen concepts except Five-Month Doubling | Five-Month Doubling | It is the only unmastered concept, and all its prerequisites are mastered. | **Provenance:** The sixteen concepts and their dependencies are copied from docs/learning-graph/learning-graph.json in this repository, restricted to Five-Month Doubling and everything it depends on. The sim must copy the values into its own folder, not read the file at run time. **Rules:** The ready set for a problem is computed by the ready rule from the table. Each problem has exactly one correct ready set. A problem is scored on its first submitted set only. The score counts first-attempt correct sets out of 6. Mastery is a score >= 5. Mastered nodes are shown as already known and cannot be selected. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the graph with the mastered concepts marked, and the problem number. 2. The learner selects every concept they judge to be ready and submits. 3. The sim marks the answer and highlights the correct ready concepts and the prerequisites that make them ready. 4. If incorrect, the learner may select again; the second attempt does not change the score. After the second attempt, the correct set and reason are shown. 5. After all 6 problems, the sim shows the score. 6. The learner should notice that the number of ready concepts rises from two to four and then falls to one as the student nears the goal. **Feedback:** 6 problems, fixed order, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct. [Why text]." Incorrect with a missing node: "At least one ready concept is missing. Check every unmastered concept's prerequisites." Incorrect with an extra node: "At least one selected concept still has an unmastered prerequisite." After the second wrong attempt the correct set is shown with the Why text. Score "n of 6" is shown at the end. **Starting State:** The full graph is shown with problem 1, no concepts mastered, and the prompt "Which concepts could this student start on?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's worked examples use the same sixteen concepts: seven layers, 15 prerequisites of Five-Month Doubling, and the ready set of AI Benchmark and Large Language Model for the mastered set of problem 3. The mastery bar is 5 of 6.
